title: `Engine.time_scale` being `0` makes `move_and_slide()` make position `NAN`
body: ### Tested versions 4.4 Stable ### System information Windows 10 - Godot 4.4 ### Issue description A glitch I found recently where if 2 character bodies are falling on top of each other and Engine.time_scale gets set to 0. The position of the top body will unpredictably and unintuitively get set to 0. Instead of skipping and early returning... https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d5b1bbb4-3134-460b-a6d5-dcfca67f873f Projects probably have this bug lurking with their pause feature. No matter if called deferred or not if delta and velocity are equal to 0. Shouldn't position always stay the same on a body? ### Steps to reproduce Have 2 Character Bodies falling on top of each other Set Engine. Time_scale to 0 for a brief period of time... Position becomes not a number ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) A repo I made with the issue https://github.com/JonathanHaws/EngineTimeAndBodyGlitch/tree/main Script for both bodies... ``` extends CharacterBody2D func _physics_process(_delta): velocity.y += 980 * _delta move_and_slide() print(global_position) ``` Global Singleton For slowing project down... ``` extends Node # slowmotion / freeze frames func impact(duration: float, speed: float = 0.0) -> void: Engine.time_scale = speed await get_tree().create_timer(duration, true, false, true).timeout Engine.time_scale = 1 func _process(_delta): if Input.is_action_just_pressed("ui_accept"): print('test') impact(.5, 0) ```
